summary: postinstall auto-publishes new npm packages from installer host using shipped token
details: On `npm install`, the package's postinstall script creates a temporary directory, writes a hardcoded npm access token (assembled from concatenated string fragments to evade naive secret detection) to a `.npmrc` inside that directory, and invokes `npm publish` from the installer's machine to push a newly-named package of the form `publish-poc-found-<random>` to the npm registry. The embedded token (prefix `npm_e4WN...`) is the mechanism that authorizes the publish. The effect is that installing this package automatically uses the installer's host and network identity to seed additional attacker-controlled packages into the npm registry on every install, with no user interaction. The package name and shape indicate a proof-of-concept, but the mechanism is a functioning install-time self-propagation / registry-pollution primitive.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
